title: The World Before It All Began
text: I suddenly snapped to attention and looked around, I say. Some kind of road… no wait, I recognized this place—it was the road where I had my lovely rendezvous with Filo-tan. So I figured I’d been flung into that particular loop, but Filo-tan was nowhere to be seen. I checked my status to confirm the Filolial-sama registered there, but there wasn’t a single one, I say. And more importantly, I was dressed in my regular clothes—the very ones I’d been wearing right after arriving in this other world.

???  What in the world was going on? Setting aside the location, I couldn’t even begin to imagine the situation, indeed. After all, right after a loop begins, I’m supposed to be able to deduce what’s happening. But this time I had absolutely no clue.

No Filolial-sama around, and Father wasn’t nearby either. The only thing I could think of was that this was before I’d raised any Filolial-sama, back when I was in the middle of acting to help Father. No, wait—even if this were the loop where I headed to Siltvelt, it should have been nighttime by now, but unfortunately it was broad daylight. And even if I’d left Éclair behind to chase after someone, the location made no sense for that either. Frankly speaking, not once in any of my previous loops had I ever ended up in a situation like this.

I needed to find some clue to work with. I checked my spear to see if there were any drop items or the like, but there was nothing. Just where on earth had that thing dropped me into a loop? I should have asked before looping. It kept saying something about a “bonus stage”—it should’ve just told me where, I say. Given how suggestively coy it was acting, there was an extremely high chance it deliberately withheld the answer. I swear I’ll turn it into an axle for something. Or maybe I’ll just stick it up that bastard’s backside? No, wait, that might end up being a reward for it. Either way, let’s gather information first and judge from there.
“Portal Spear!”
And so, as a first step, I decided to warp over to Melromarc.

Having arrived in Melromarc, I checked out the castle town, I say. Nothing in particular seemed to have changed. Storming straight into the castle to threaten Trash was certainly an option, but if I made a scene needlessly, Father might scold me for it. So instead, playing the part of a scout, I went cloaked to check the inside of the castle. Hmm… I couldn’t quite make sense of things.

Oh? I spotted Trash inside the castle. Where might the Crimson Swine be, I wondered. Striking first and beating it to death might not be a bad idea either. Thinking that, I followed Trash, and… it seemed he was heading somewhere like a meeting room to talk with someone.
“The long school holidays are coming up soon, and Malty will be coming home. She’s written asking for a meal made with some rare ingredients, so I intend to have it prepared.”
The other person was… who, exactly? Someone I felt I’d seen before, and yet hadn’t—someone strangely familiar despite feeling like a first meeting.
“What of it? Are you telling me even this much is too much to ask!”
Trash was speaking in a tone like he was trying to gauge the other person’s mood.
“You too have a daughter, do you not? Are you saying even that much isn’t permitted for me!”
“……Understood. I shall prepare it. I’ll ask someone from my territory if they’re able to go out fishing.”
“Good! I leave it to you. Ahh, I do so wish to see that girl’s face again soon.”
Trash seemed satisfied with the response. And then, as the other person left the room… oh? There seemed to be Éclair standing in front of the room.
It looked as though she was awaiting orders.
“This time I will go myself. I must make the request knowing full well it’s an imposition. You stay here at the castle.”
“Yes, sir!”
And Éclair obediently followed the order, it seemed.
“You’re finally returning to your territory. Please, do take some time to rest your wings a while.”
At Éclair’s words, the person appeared to smile.
“Ah, I mustn’t be away too long, but I suppose I’ll allow myself to stretch my wings a little.”

Hmm…? If Éclair was walking around the castle so naturally, did that mean this was after the whole Three Heroes Church incident? No, wait—it’s possible I’d landed in some peaceful stretch of time after Trash had reformed, back before the whole wave business even started. I searched the castle but found no sign of my Fiancée anywhere. Something wasn’t quite adding up, so I decided to head over to the village in Father’s territory. If it were after peace had been restored, that village should generally have been in the process of being rebuilt by now. If it hadn’t been, that would raise the possibility this was the loop where I’d headed to Siltvelt. After all, that was back before I’d confirmed Big Sister was even alive. And so, I headed for Father’s territory—which doubled as Big Sister’s village.
“Welcome. Are you a traveler?”

When I arrived at Big Sister’s village, there were people who looked like villagers. Had there been villagers like this before? There were a few faces scattered about that I didn’t recognize. But it’s not unusual for me to run into personnel I don’t know, so I responded without incident.
“Just passing through, I say.”
“I see. It’s a small village, but please, take your time.”

Saying that, the villager left, somewhat wary. I strolled about the village at a leisurely pace, checking things out along the way. Hmm…? For a village that had supposedly been rebuilt, there were some fairly old buildings around. I had no idea just what point in time I’d been looped into. How long had it been since the wave occurred?
“Excuse me, I say.”
“Yes? What is it, traveler?”
It bothered me a little, but I asked anyway without minding it.
“How long has it been since the wave occurred, I wonder?”
“Huh? What do you mean by ‘wave’? Do you mean when the sea got a little rough the other day?”
……? Somehow, the conversation wasn’t lining up at all.
“Then, do you happen to know where Father… the Shield Hero is?”
“The Shield Hero-sama? He’s a legendary figure I’d dearly love to meet. I’m sure he’s watching over us from somewhere.”

Was this reaction one of simply not knowing? It sounded like nothing more than a plain religious, god-like sentiment. Spirit of the spear, just where in the world had you dropped me? The distant future, perhaps? No, surely there weren’t lookalikes of Trash and Éclair running around in the future?
“Hello there!”
“Yes, yes. Hello, Raphtalia-chan.”
Just then, off to the side of that conversation, a young Big Sister came bounding by cheerfully.
“Boo-boo!”
“Yoohoo!”

There stood Keel and Big Sister’s Friend, both looking small and young. Well, there was nothing particularly strange about them appearing so young. But… none of the villagers seemed to have any clue what the wave even was.
“Boo-boo! Boo-bee?”
“Ball games!”
“Tag!”
“Swimming in the sea sounds good too!”
“Boo-boo!”
“Boo!”
And so Keel and the others decided what to play and headed off toward the outskirts of the village.
“Hey there, Raphtalia. It’s good you’re full of energy, but don’t wander off too far, all right?”
“Ah, Papa. Okay!”

And… there stood an adult man of the same kin as Big Sister, waving with a warm, gentle smile. ……? Big Sister called him Papa……? Looking at him, there was no mistaking the blood tie—the ears, the tail, the shape of his face all bore a clear resemblance to Big Sister. But… I’d heard that Big Sister’s real parents had died in the wave. Startled, I checked the time until the wave’s arrival.

The wave hadn’t happened yet… no, could it be that it was about to happen?! In other words, it seemed I had ended up here… before this world had even become aware of the waves at all. In a loop where even Father hadn’t been summoned yet, what on earth was I supposed to do?!
